# Postmortem: checkout-api outage, 2026-10-06

**Severity:** SEV1 · **Duration:** 4h 00m (13:50–17:50 UTC) · **Status:** resolved, remediations open

## Summary

`risk-score`, a service that `checkout-api` calls synchronously during checkout, became slow without returning errors. `checkout-api` made that call inside a database transaction with no explicit timeout, so each checkout held a database connection for up to 30 s instead of the usual ~120 ms. Every pod's connection pool was exhausted within seconds, and all endpoints on the service failed, including those that never call `risk-score`.

## Impact

- `checkout-api` 5xx rate peaked at 94% and stayed above 60% for the full four hours.
- All endpoints were affected: checkout, cart view and order status.
- From 14:50 to 15:15, `orders` and `inventory` also failed to get database connections, as a side effect of a mitigation attempt.
- [N] failed checkouts, [$X] estimated lost revenue, [N] support tickets.
- No data loss or corruption; held transactions rolled back cleanly.

## Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:40 | `risk-score` p99 latency rises from 120 ms to 25–30 s after a replica failover on its datastore. It returns no errors, so its error-rate alerts stay silent. |
| 13:47 | `checkout-api` pool acquire wait climbs; first `could not acquire connection within 5s` errors. |
| 13:50 | 5xx rate crosses 5%. **Impact begins.** |
| 13:52 | 5xx alert pages on-call. |
| 13:58 | On-call acknowledges, sees pool timeout errors and suspects the database. |
| 14:00 | Pods start failing liveness probes (the probe queries the database) and restarting. Each restart briefly frees connections, producing a sawtooth error rate that looks like an intermittent database fault. |
| 14:10 | SEV1 declared and database team paged. Postgres is at 12% CPU with no slow queries; `checkout-api` connections are at their cap. |
| 14:25 | The 11:15 deploy is rolled back on suspicion. No change. |
| 14:50 | `checkout-api` scaled from 12 to 24 pods to add capacity. Its connection demand goes from 240 to 480, pushing Postgres past `max_connections` (500). `orders` and `inventory` begin failing. |
| 15:05 | Scale-up reverted. |
| 15:15 | `orders` and `inventory` recover. |
| 16:10 | `pg_stat_activity` shows the connections are `idle in transaction`. Thread dumps show the request threads blocked on socket reads to `risk-score`, and traces show 30 s spans on that call. **Root cause identified.** |
| 16:20 | `risk-score` team paged; they confirm elevated latency since 13:40. |
| 16:35 | No kill switch exists for the call. Team decides on a hotfix: a 2 s timeout, failing open to the manual review queue (approved by the risk lead). |
| 17:20 | Hotfix on canary; pool wait on canary pods drops to baseline. |
| 17:40 | Hotfix fully rolled out. |
| 17:50 | 5xx rate back to baseline. **Impact ends.** |
| 18:05 | `risk-score` latency recovers independently. |
| 18:30 | Incident closed. |

## Root cause

The checkout handler opens a database transaction, calls `risk-score` over HTTP, then writes the order and commits. The connection is held for the whole downstream call. The HTTP client had no configured timeout and used the library default of 30 s.

Each pod has a pool of 20 connections and handles about 5 checkouts per second. At a 120 ms hold time that needs about one connection. At 30 s it needs about 150, so the pool saturated in roughly four seconds and stayed saturated. Every other request on the pod then queued for a connection and failed after the 5 s acquire timeout.

Contributing factors:

- **No bulkhead.** All endpoints share one pool, so a checkout-only dependency took down read-only endpoints.
- **Liveness probe depends on the database.** Pool exhaustion made healthy pods look dead, and the restarts added churn and obscured the signal.
- **No kill switch.** Bypassing `risk-score` required a code change and deploy.
- **Alerting gaps.** `risk-score` alerted on error rate but not latency. `checkout-api` had no alert on pool saturation or on downstream call latency.

## Why recovery took four hours

Detection took 2 minutes, diagnosis took 2h 18m, and the fix took 1h 40m.

Diagnosis was slow because the error message named the database, and the runbook for pool timeouts covers only database causes. The dependency dashboard showed `risk-score` green because it reports error rate only. Nobody looked at what the connections were doing until 16:10. The scale-up at 14:50 followed the same wrong model and widened the outage.

The fix was slow because there was no way to disable or time-bound the call without shipping code.

## Remediations

| # | Action | Owner | Due | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Explicit 2 s timeout on the `risk-score` call, failing open to manual review | Checkout | done 10-06 | Shipped as hotfix |
| 2 | Move the `risk-score` call outside the database transaction | Checkout | 10-16 | In progress |
| 3 | Circuit breaker and runtime kill switch on the `risk-score` call | Checkout | 10-23 | Open |
| 4 | Audit all outbound HTTP clients in `checkout-api` for missing timeouts; add a lint rule that rejects clients without one | Checkout | 10-23 | Open |
| 5 | Separate connection pool for checkout writes so read endpoints survive | Checkout | 10-30 | Open |
| 6 | Liveness probe stops querying the database; database check moves to readiness only | Checkout | 10-16 | Open |
| 7 | Alerts on pool acquire wait p99 and pool utilisation above 80% | Checkout | 10-16 | Open |
| 8 | Latency SLO and p99 alert on `risk-score`; add latency to the dependency dashboard | Risk | 10-23 | Open |
| 9 | Per-service Postgres connection limits so one service cannot exhaust `max_connections` | Database | 10-30 | Open |
| 10 | Update the pool timeout runbook: check `pg_stat_activity` for `idle in transaction` and trace downstream latency first; do not scale out | SRE | 10-13 | Open |
| 11 | Set `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` on the `checkout-api` database role | Database | 10-16 | Open |

Items 2, 3 and 6 are the ones that would have prevented or sharply shortened this incident; the hotfix in item 1 only bounds the hold time.
